title: 大智度論
text: 「舍利弗！置閻浮提滿中如舍利弗、目連等。若滿三千大千世界如舍利弗、目連等；復置是事，若滿十方如恒河沙等世界如舍利弗、目連等智慧，欲比菩薩行般若波羅蜜智慧，百分不及一，千分百千分乃至算數譬喻所不能及。」
left: "Śāriputra, set aside the Jambudvīpa (Jambudvīpa) filled with beings like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana. If you were to fill the entire tri-sāhasra-mahat-sāhasra-lokadhātu (tri-sāhasra-mahat-sāhasra-lokadhātu) with beings like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and furthermore, set aside that matter and fill the ten directions (daśan-diś) with world systems (lokadhātu) as numerous as the sands of the Ganges (gaṅgā-nadī-vālikā) with beings possessing the wisdom (jñāna) of Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and if one wished to compare this to the wisdom of a bodhisattva (bodhisattva) practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), it would not reach a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor could it be reached by any calculation (gaṇanā) or analogy (upamā)."
right: "Śāriputra! Set aside the whole of Jambudvīpa filled with beings like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana. If you were to fill the entire great trichiliocosm (trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu) with beings like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana; and furthermore, set aside that matter, and if you were to fill world systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, with the wisdom of beings like Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, and wished to compare it to the wisdom of a bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), it would not reach a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, or even any part reachable by calculation or analogy."

title: 大智度論
text: 佛告須菩提：「菩薩摩訶薩念般若波羅蜜，如般若波羅蜜中說，行是道，一念頃超越劫數，亦如彼人一日一夜心念之數。是菩薩摩訶薩行般若波羅蜜，遠離眾罪，所謂離阿耨多羅三藐三菩提罪。是菩薩摩訶薩行般若波羅蜜，一日所得善根功德，假令滿如恒河沙等三千大千世界中餘功德，猶亦不減；於餘殘功德，百分不及一分，千分千億萬分，乃至算數譬喻所不能及。」
left: The Buddha said to Subhūti: "A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (great being) who contemplates the Prajñāpāramitā (perfection of wisdom), as it is taught within the Prajñāpāramitā, and who practices this path, transcends the count of aeons in a single moment of thought, just as a person might count the thoughts of a single day and night. This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, practicing the Prajñāpāramitā, remains far from all transgressions, which is to say, he remains far from the transgression of failing to attain the Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi (unsurpassed complete awakening). When this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the Prajñāpāramitā, the Kuśala-mūla (wholesome roots) and Guṇa (merit) obtained in a single day are such that, even if one were to fill the Tri-sāhasra-mahat-sāhasra-lokadhātu (three-thousand-great-thousand world systems) with other merits, his merit would not be diminished; compared to those remaining merits, they do not reach even one part in a hundred, nor one in a thousand, a hundred thousand, or ten million, and they cannot be reached by any calculation or analogy."
right: The Buddha said to Subhūti, "A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (great being) who contemplates the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), as it is taught within the Perfection of Wisdom, and who practices this path, transcends the count of eons in a single moment of thought, just as a person might count the thoughts of a day and a night. This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, practicing the Perfection of Wisdom, remains far from all transgressions, which is to say, he remains far from the transgression of failing to attain Unsurpassed Perfect Awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi). When this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the Perfection of Wisdom, the roots of merit (kuśalamūla) and virtues (puṇya) obtained in a single day are such that, even if one were to fill the three-thousand-great-thousand-fold world systems with other virtues equal to the sands of the Ganges, they would not diminish; compared to these remaining virtues, those others do not reach even one part in a hundred, nor one in a thousand, a hundred thousand, or ten million, and they cannot be reached by any calculation or analogy."

title: 大智度論
text: 佛言：「如是！如是！須菩提！不可說義無增無減。菩薩摩訶薩習行般若波羅蜜，有方便力故，不作是念：『我增般若波羅蜜，乃至增檀波羅蜜。』當作是念：『但名字故，名檀波羅蜜。』是菩薩摩訶薩行檀波羅蜜時，是心及善根，如阿耨多羅三藐三菩提相迴向；乃至行般若波羅蜜時，是心及善根，如阿耨多羅三藐三菩提相迴向。」
left: The Buddha said: "So it is! So it is, Subhūti! The inexpressible meaning is without increase and without decrease. When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (great being) practices the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), because of the power of skillful means (upāya), he does not think: 'I increase the Perfection of Wisdom, or even increase the Perfection of Giving (dānapāramitā).' He should think: 'It is only because of a name that it is called the Perfection of Giving.' When this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the Perfection of Giving, he directs this mind and these roots of merit toward the characteristics of Unsurpassed Perfect Awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi); and even when practicing the Perfection of Wisdom, he directs this mind and these roots of merit toward the characteristics of Unsurpassed Perfect Awakening."
right: The Buddha said: "So it is, Subhūti! So it is! The meaning of the inexpressible (anabhilāpya) is neither increased nor decreased. When a bodhisattva mahāsattva (bodhisattva mahāsattva) trains in the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), because of the power of skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), he does not think: 'I increase the perfection of wisdom, and so on, up to increasing the perfection of giving (dāna-pāramitā).' He should think: 'It is only because of a name (nāman) that it is called the perfection of giving.' When this bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving, he directs (pariṇāmay) this mind and these roots of goodness (kuśala-mūla) toward the aspect of supreme perfect enlightenment (samyaksambodhi); and so on, up to when he practices the perfection of wisdom, he directs this mind and these roots of goodness toward the aspect of supreme perfect enlightenment."

title: 大智度論
text: 佛告須菩提：「若菩薩摩訶薩如是知一切法性自離、一切法性自空，非聲聞、辟支佛作，亦非佛作；諸法相常住、法相、法住、法位、如、實際，是名菩薩行般若波羅蜜不離薩婆若念。何以故？般若波羅蜜性自離、性自空，不增不減故。」
left: The Buddha said to Subhūti, "If a bodhisattva mahāsattva (great being) thus knows that the nature of all dharmas (phenomena) is inherently detached and that the nature of all dharmas is inherently empty—not created by a śrāvaka (disciple), not created by a pratyekabuddha (solitary buddha), and also not created by a Buddha—and that the characteristics of all dharmas are eternally abiding (nitya), the dharma-lakṣaṇa (characteristic of phenomena), the dharma-sthiti (abiding of phenomena), the dharma-niyāmatā (fixed position of phenomena), suchness, and the reality-limit, this is called the bodhisattva-caryā (bodhisattva practice) of the prajñāpāramitā (perfection of wisdom) without departing from the sarva-ākārajña (omniscience) mindfulness. Why is this? Because the nature of the prajñāpāramitā is inherently detached and inherently empty, for it neither increases nor decreases."
right: The Buddha said to Subhūti: "If a bodhisattva mahāsattva (great being) thus knows that the nature of all phenomena (dharma) is inherently detached and that the nature of all phenomena is inherently empty, not created by a voice-hearer (śrāvaka) nor by a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddha), and also not created by a buddha; if he knows that the characteristics of all phenomena are eternally abiding, the dharma-characteristic (dharmalakṣaṇa), the dharma-abiding (dharmasthiti), the dharma-position (dharmaniyāma), suchness (tathatā), and the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), this is called the bodhisattva practicing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) without departing from the thought of omniscience (sarvajñatā). Why is this? Because the nature of the perfection of wisdom is inherently detached and inherently empty, for it neither increases nor decreases."

title: 大智度論
text: 言無有餘福德如菩薩摩訶薩力勢者，是中自說因緣：「菩薩行般若時，得諸法平等忍；得平等忍故，雖行空，亦能生四無量心。」四無量心中，大悲是大乘之本；見眾生就於死法，如囚受戮。諸菩薩能生六波羅蜜等乃至一切種智，是故諸菩薩能生大悲。
left: Regarding the statement that there is no other merit equal to the power and influence of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, the cause and condition for this is explained therein: "When a bodhisattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), he attains the patience (kṣānti) of the equality of all phenomena (dharma). Because he attains this patience of equality, although he practices emptiness (śūnyatā), he is also able to give rise to the four immeasurables (apramāṇa). Among the four immeasurables, great compassion (mahākaruṇā) is the root of the great vehicle (mahāyāna); he sees sentient beings approaching the phenomena of death, like prisoners awaiting execution. Bodhisattvas are able to give rise to the six perfections (pāramitā) and so on, up to the omniscience of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā); it is for this reason that bodhisattvas are able to give rise to great compassion."
right: Regarding the statement that there is no other merit (puṇya) equal to the power and influence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva (bodhisattva mahāsattva), the reason is explained therein: "When a bodhisattva practices wisdom (prajñā), he attains the patience (kṣānti) of the equality of all phenomena (dharma); because he attains this patience of equality, although he practices emptiness (śūnyatā), he is also able to give rise to the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa)." Among the four immeasurables, great compassion (mahat-karuṇā) is the root of the great vehicle (mahāyāna); he sees beings approaching the law of death, like prisoners awaiting execution. All bodhisattvas are able to give rise to the six perfections (ṣaṣ-pāramitā) and so forth, up to and including the knowledge of all aspects (sarva-ākāra-jña); it is for this reason that all bodhisattvas are able to give rise to great compassion.

title: 大智度論
text: 佛言：「阿難！不如弟子以般若波羅蜜相應法為菩薩摩訶薩說，乃至一日，其福多！置一日，但半日；置半日，但一食頃；置一食頃，但須臾間說，其福多！何以故？菩薩摩訶薩善根勝一切聲聞、辟支佛故。菩薩摩訶薩自欲得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，亦示、教、利、喜他人，令得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。阿難！如是菩薩行六波羅蜜，行四念處乃至行一切種智，增益善根，若不得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，無有是處！」
left: The Buddha said: "Ānanda, if a disciple were to teach a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (great being) the doctrine corresponding to the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), even for a single day, the merit would be great. Setting aside a day, even for half a day; setting aside half a day, even for the duration of a single meal; setting aside the duration of a single meal, even for a brief moment of teaching, the merit would be great. Why is this? Because the wholesome roots (kuśala-mūla) of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva surpass those of all Hearers (śrāvaka) and Solitary Buddhas (pratyekabuddha). A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva desires to attain the Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) for himself, and he also demonstrates, instructs, benefits, and gladdens others, causing them to attain the Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment. Ānanda, in this way, a Bodhisattva practicing the six Perfections (pāramitā), practicing the four Establishments of Mindfulness (smṛti-upasthāna), and even practicing the Knowledge of All Aspects (sarva-ākārajña), increases his wholesome roots; that he should not attain the Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment is an impossibility."
right: The Buddha said: "Ānanda, if a disciple were to teach a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva (great being) the doctrine corresponding to the Perfection of Wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) for even a single day, the merit would be great. Setting aside a day, even for half a day; setting aside half a day, even for the duration of a single meal; setting aside the duration of a single meal, even for a mere moment of teaching, the merit is great. Why is this? Because the wholesome roots (kuśalamūla) of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva surpass those of all Hearers (śrāvaka) and Solitary Buddhas (pratyekabuddha). A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva desires to attain Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) for himself, and he also demonstrates, instructs, benefits, and gladdens others, causing them to attain Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment. Ānanda, that a Bodhisattva who thus practices the six Perfections (pāramitā), practices the four Establishments of Mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna), and even practices the Omniscience of all aspects (sarvajñatā), thereby increasing his wholesome roots, would not attain Unsurpassed, Right and Perfect Enlightenment—such a situation does not exist."

title: 大智度論
text: 「是菩薩以天耳淨，過於人耳，聞二種聲：天聲、人聲。亦不著是天耳神通，天耳與聲及己身皆不可得，自性空故、自性離故、自性無生故。不作是念：『我有是天耳。』除為薩婆若心。如是，舍利弗！菩薩摩訶薩行般若波羅蜜時，得天耳神通智證。
left: "The bodhisattva, by means of the purity of the divine ear (divya-śrotra), surpassing that of humans, hears two kinds of sounds: divine sounds and human sounds. He does not become attached to this supernormal power (abhijñā) of the divine ear; the divine ear, the sounds, and his own body are all unattainable, because their self-nature (svabhāva) is empty (śūnyatā), because their self-nature is detached, and because their self-nature is non-arising (anutpāda). He does not form this thought: 'I possess this divine ear,' except for the sake of the mind of omniscience (sarva-ākārajña). Thus, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), he attains the realization of the supernormal knowledge (abhijñā-jñāna) of the divine ear."
right: "That bodhisattva (bodhisattva), with the purity of the divine ear (divyaśrotra), surpassing human hearing, hears two kinds of sounds: divine sounds and human sounds. He does not become attached to this supernormal power (abhijñā) of the divine ear; the divine ear, the sounds, and his own body are all unattainable, because their self-nature (svabhāva) is empty, because their self-nature is detached, and because their self-nature is non-arising. He does not entertain the thought: 'I possess this divine ear,' except for the sake of the mind of omniscience (sarvajñatā). Thus, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva (mahāsattva) practices the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), he attains the realization of the wisdom of the supernormal power of the divine ear."

title: 大智度論
text: 爾時，須菩提及大眾歡喜讚歎般若波羅蜜，作是言：「大波羅蜜，所謂般若波羅蜜。」大波羅蜜者，所謂一切法雖自性空，而般若波羅蜜能利益菩薩，令得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提；雖得，亦無所得；雖轉法輪，亦無所轉。
left: At that time, Subhūti and the great assembly rejoiced and praised the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), saying: "The great perfection (mahāpāramitā), that is to say, the perfection of wisdom." The great perfection is that which, although all phenomena (dharma) are empty in their own-nature (svabhāva), the perfection of wisdom is able to benefit the bodhisattva, causing them to attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening (anuttarasamyaksambodhi); yet, although they attain it, there is no attainment; although they turn the wheel of the dharma (dharmacakra), there is no turning.
right: At that time, Subhūti and the great assembly rejoiced and praised the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), saying: "The great perfection, that is to say, the perfection of wisdom." The great perfection is that which, although all phenomena (sarva-dharma) are empty of intrinsic nature (svabhāva-śūnyatā), the perfection of wisdom is able to benefit the bodhisattva, enabling them to attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening (anuttarasamyaksambodhi); although they attain it, there is no attainment (anupalambha); although they turn the wheel of the dharma, there is nothing turned.

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 又諸行中，無常、無恒、無不變易。此諸行中，常、恒、不變無性，非有為攝、非無為攝，共相觀識非不緣此境界而轉。若緣此境識不轉者，便於諸行常、恒、不變無性之中，不能如實智慧觀察。若不觀察，應不生厭；若不生厭，應不離欲；若不離欲，應無解脫；若無解脫，應無永盡究竟涅槃。若有此理，一切有情應皆究竟隨逐雜染，無出離期。是名第四言論道理。
left: Furthermore, among all conditioned phenomena (saṃskāra), there is impermanence (anitya), lack of constancy, and lack of immutability. Within these conditioned phenomena, the nature of permanence, constancy, and immutability is non-existent; they are neither included in the compounded (saṃskṛta) nor included in the uncompounded (asaṃskṛta). The consciousness that observes their common characteristics does not turn away from taking this domain (viṣaya) as its object. If the consciousness were not to turn toward this domain, then one would be unable to observe, with wisdom (prajñā) as it truly is (yathābhūtam), the non-existence of permanence, constancy, and immutability within all conditioned phenomena. If one does not observe this, one should not experience revulsion; if one does not experience revulsion, one should not become dispassionate; if one does not become dispassionate, there should be no liberation (vimukti); if there is no liberation, there should be no ultimate (niṣṭhā) and final nirvana (nirvāṇa). If this logic (yukti) were the case, all sentient beings (sarva-sattva) would necessarily follow defilement forever, with no time for departure. This is called the fourth principle of discourse.
right: Furthermore, among all compounded phenomena (saṃskāra), there is impermanence, instability, and change. Within these compounded phenomena, the nature of permanence, stability, and immutability is non-existent; it is not included among the compounded (saṃskṛta), nor is it included among the uncompounded (asaṃskṛta). The consciousness that observes the common characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇa) does not turn without taking this state of affairs as its object. If, by taking this object, consciousness were not to turn, then one would be unable to observe according to reality (yathābhūta) with wisdom (prajñā) the non-existence of permanence, stability, and immutability within all compounded phenomena. If one does not observe, one should not experience revulsion (nirveda); if one does not experience revulsion, one should not become dispassionate (virāga); if one does not become dispassionate, one should not attain liberation (vimukti); if one does not attain liberation, one should not attain the ultimate, eternal cessation, which is nirvana (nirvāṇa). If this principle were true, all sentient beings (sattva) would ultimately remain subject to defilement (saṃkleśa) forever, with no time for emergence. This is called the fourth principle of discourse (yukti).

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 復於所餘不同分界不現見蘊，比度觀察。謂彼所有，有為、有漏，遍一切處、遍一切種，於一切時，皆有如是法、皆墮如是理、皆有如是性。彼所有滅，皆永寂靜，常住安樂。彼所有道，皆能永斷，究竟出離。
left: Furthermore, regarding the remaining aggregates (skandha) that are not manifest in different realms, one should observe them through inference. It is said that whatever is conditioned (saṃskṛta) and tainted (sāsrava) is, in every place, in every mode, and at all times, possessed of such a nature, subject to such a principle, and characterized by such a quality. Whatever cessation (nirodha) there is for them is forever tranquil, permanently abiding, and blissful. Whatever path (mārga) there is for them is capable of forever cutting off and leads to ultimate departure.
right: Furthermore, regarding the remaining aggregates (skandha) that are not of the same category (sabhāga) and are not directly perceived (pratyakṣa), one should observe them through inference. That is to say, whatever is conditioned (saṃskṛta) and tainted (āsrava) among them, in all places (sarvatra) and in all modes (sarva-ākāra), at all times, all possess such phenomena, all fall under such principles, and all possess such a nature. Whatever cessation (nirodha) they possess is forever tranquil, permanently abiding (nitya), and blissful (sukha). Whatever path (mārga) they possess is capable of forever abandoning (prahāṇa) and is the ultimate (niṣṭhā) departure.

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 復次，如先所說作及增長業，若先所說由五因緣成極重業，名定受業。與此相違，名不定受業。復有四業。一、異熟定，二、時分定，三、二俱定，四、二俱不定。諸阿羅漢所有不善決定受業，或於前生所作，或於此生先異生位所作，由少輕苦之所逼惱，便名果報已熟。若已轉依，果報種子皆永斷故，一切不受。所以者何？由佛世尊依未解脫相續，建立定受業故。
left: Furthermore, as previously stated regarding action (karman) that is performed and accumulated, if, as previously stated, it becomes extremely heavy due to five causes and conditions, it is called action that is certainly to be experienced (niyatavedanīya-karman). What is contrary to this is called action that is not certainly to be experienced (aniyatavedanīya-karman). There are also four [other] kinds of action: first, certainty of ripening (vipāka-niyata); second, certainty of time (kāla-niyata); third, certainty of both; and fourth, uncertainty of both. Regarding all unwholesome action that is certainly to be experienced possessed by an arhat (arhat)—whether performed in a previous life or performed in this life while still in the state of an ordinary person (pṛthagjana)—it is said that the fruit (vipāka) has ripened when they are afflicted by a small and light suffering. If they have already attained the transformation of the basis (āśraya-parāvṛtti), because the seeds (bīja) of the fruit are forever severed, they do not experience any of it. For what reason? Because the Buddha, the Blessed One, established [the doctrine of] action that is certainly to be experienced in reliance upon the continuum (saṃtāna) of those who are not yet liberated.
right: Furthermore, as previously stated regarding action (karman) that is performed and accumulated, if, as previously stated, it becomes extremely heavy due to five causes and conditions, it is called action that is certainly to be experienced (niyatavedanīya-karman). What is contrary to this is called action that is not certainly to be experienced (aniyatavedanīya-karman). There are also four [other] kinds of action: first, certainty of ripening (vipāka-niyata); second, certainty of time (kāla-niyata); third, certainty of both; and fourth, uncertainty of both. Regarding all the unwholesome action that is certainly to be experienced possessed by an Arhant (arhant)—whether performed in a previous life or performed in this life while previously in the state of an ordinary person (pṛthagjana)—it is called "ripened fruit" (vipāka-phala) when they are afflicted by a small, light suffering. If they have already attained transformation of the basis (āśraya-parāvṛtti), because the seeds (bīja) of the fruit are all eternally severed, they do not experience any of it. For what reason? Because the Buddha Bhagavant (buddha bhagavant) established action that is certainly to be experienced based upon a continuum (saṃtāna) that is not yet liberated (vimukta).

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 云何菩薩具於善行？此何行相？謂諸菩薩，於內成熟諸佛法故，於外成熟諸有情故，修行善行，是故說名具於善行。當知此行有七行相。一者、無所依止而惠施故；二者、無所依止而持戒故；三者、由哀愍心而修忍故；四者、非於少分修精進故；五者、為作利益諸有情處修靜慮故；六者、見不相應修妙慧故；七者、成熟方便善巧故。
left: How does a bodhisattva (bodhisattva) possess good practice (kuśala-dharma)? What is the nature of this practice? It is because bodhisattvas cultivate good practice in order to mature all Buddha-dharmas (buddha-dharma) internally and to mature all sentient beings (sattva) externally; therefore, it is said that they possess good practice. One should know that this practice has seven aspects: first, giving without any support (āśraya); second, observing morality (śīla) without any support; third, cultivating patience (kṣānti) out of a compassionate heart; fourth, cultivating vigor (vīrya) not merely in a small measure; fifth, cultivating meditative absorption (dhyāna) for the sake of benefiting sentient beings; sixth, cultivating profound wisdom (prajñā) by seeing what is not associated (viprayuj); and seventh, the maturity of skill in means (upāya-kauśalya).
right: How does a bodhisattva (bodhisattva) possess good practice (kuśaladharma-caryā)? What is the nature of this practice? It is because bodhisattvas cultivate good practice in order to mature the Buddha-dharmas (buddhadharma) internally and to mature sentient beings (sattva) externally; therefore, they are said to possess good practice. One should know that this practice has seven aspects: first, giving (dāna) without any reliance; second, maintaining morality (śīla) without any reliance; third, cultivating patience (kṣānti) out of a heart of compassion (karuṇā); fourth, cultivating vigor (vīrya) not just in a small measure; fifth, cultivating meditative absorption (dhyāna) for the sake of benefiting sentient beings; sixth, cultivating transcendent wisdom (prajñā) by seeing that which is not corresponding; and seventh, the skill in means (upāya-kauśalya) of maturation.

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 復次，建立極微，當知有五種勝利。謂由分析一合聚色安立方便，於所緣境便能清淨廣大修習，是初勝利。又能漸斷薩迦耶見，是第二勝利。如能漸斷薩迦耶見，如是亦能漸斷憍慢，是第三勝利。又能漸伏諸煩惱纏，是第四勝利。又能速疾除遣諸相，是第五勝利。如是等類，應當如理思惟極微。
left: Furthermore, in establishing the subtle atom (paramāṇu), one should know there are five kinds of advantages (anuśaṃsa). By means of the method (upāya) of analyzing the composite form, one is able to practice purely and extensively upon the object of perception (ālambana); this is the first advantage. Furthermore, one is able to gradually abandon the view of a self-existent body (satkāyadṛṣṭi); this is the second advantage. Just as one is able to gradually abandon the view of a self-existent body, so too is one able to gradually abandon arrogance (māna); this is the third advantage. Furthermore, one is able to gradually subdue all the fetters of the defilements (kleśa); this is the fourth advantage. Furthermore, one is able to quickly dispel all marks (nimitta); this is the fifth advantage. Regarding such matters as these, one should reflect appropriately (yoniśomanasikāra).
right: Furthermore, regarding the establishment of the subtle atom (paramāṇu), one should know there are five kinds of advantages. By means of the method of analyzing the composite form (rūpa), one is able to practice purely and extensively upon the object of perception (ālambana); this is the first advantage. Furthermore, one is able to gradually sever the view of self-identity (satkāyadṛṣṭi); this is the second advantage. Just as one is able to gradually sever the view of self-identity, so too is one able to gradually sever arrogance (māna); this is the third advantage. Furthermore, one is able to gradually subdue all the fetters of defilement (kleśaparyavasthāna); this is the fourth advantage. Furthermore, one is able to quickly dispel all marks (nimitta); this is the fifth advantage. In this way and others, one should contemplate the subtle atom according to reality.

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 答：若已與果種子相續，名過去界；若未與果，當來種子相續，名未來界；若未與果，現在種子相續，名現在界。當知此中如是密意。若苾芻等於如是種子相續中而得善巧，名於彼彼一切法中證得無量種種自性諸界善巧。
left: The answer is: If a continuum of seeds (bīja) has already produced a fruit (phala), it is called the past realm (atīta-dhātu); if it has not yet produced a fruit and the continuum of seeds is for the future, it is called the future realm (anāgata-dhātu); if it has not yet produced a fruit and the continuum of seeds is present, it is called the present realm (pratyutpanna-dhātu). You should know that this is the hidden intention (abhisandhi) here. If a monk (bhikṣu) attains skill (kauśalya) in such a continuum of seeds, he is said to have attained, in those various phenomena (sarva-dharma), skill in the immeasurable and various self-natures (svabhāva) of all realms.
right: The answer is: If a continuum of seeds (bīja) has already produced a fruit (phala), it is called the past realm (atīta-dhātu); if it has not yet produced a fruit, but the continuum of seeds is directed toward the future, it is called the future realm (anāgata-dhātu); if it has not yet produced a fruit, but the continuum of seeds is present, it is called the present realm (pratyutpanna-dhātu). You should understand the hidden meaning (abhisandhi) here in this way. If a monk (bhikṣu) or others attain skill (kauśalya) in such a continuum of seeds, they are said to have attained, in all these various phenomena (dharma), skill in the various realms (dhātu) of infinite and diverse natures (svabhāva).

title: 雜阿含經
text: 「復次，聚落主！有受欲樂者，以法求財，不以濫取，以樂自供，供養父母，給足兄弟、妻子、奴婢、眷屬、知識，隨時供養沙門、婆羅門，仰求勝處安樂果報，未來生天，是名第三受欲樂者。
left: "Furthermore, village headman! There is one who enjoys sensual pleasures (kāma-bhoga) who seeks wealth in accordance with the Dharma (dharma), not by illicit means, and uses that wealth to provide for his own happiness, to support his parents, to provide for his brothers, wife, children, servants, dependents, and acquaintances, and to make offerings at the proper times to ascetics (śramaṇa) and priests (brāhmaṇa), looking upward to a superior place and a fruit of happiness, and to birth in heaven in the future; this is called the third type of one who enjoys sensual pleasures."
right: "Furthermore, village headman, there is the one who experiences the pleasures of desire who seeks wealth in accordance with the Dharma (dharma), not by improper means. With that wealth, he provides for his own happiness, makes offerings (pūjā) to his parents, and provides for his brothers, wife and children (putra-dāra), servants, attendants (parivāra), and friends (mitra). He makes offerings at the proper times to ascetics (śramaṇa) and brahmins (brāhmaṇa), looking upward to a superior state, a fruit of happiness (sukha), and a future (anāgata) birth in heaven. This is called the third type of person who experiences the pleasures of desire."

title: 雜阿含經
text: 佛告舍利弗：「若彼比丘諂曲幻偽、欺誑、不信、無慚無愧、懈怠失念、不定惡慧、慢緩、違於遠離、不敬戒律、不顧沙門行、不求涅槃、為命出家。如是比丘不應教授，與共言語。所以者何？此等比丘破梵行故。若彼比丘不諂曲、不幻偽、不欺誑、信心、慚愧、精勤正念、正定智慧、不慢緩、心存遠離、深敬戒律、顧沙門行、志崇涅槃、為法出家。如是比丘應當教授。所以者何？如是比丘能修梵行，能自建立故。」
left: The Buddha said to Śāriputra: “If a bhikṣu is devious, deceitful, fraudulent, faithless, lacking in shame and moral dread, lazy, lacking in mindfulness (smṛti), unstable, of evil wisdom (prajñā), sluggish, averse to seclusion, disrespectful of the precepts (śikṣāpada), unconcerned with the conduct of a śramaṇa, and does not seek nirvāṇa, but has gone forth (pravrajyā) for the sake of his livelihood—such a bhikṣu should not be instructed or spoken with. For what reason? Because such bhikṣus destroy the holy life (brahmacarya). If a bhikṣu is not devious, not deceitful, not fraudulent, possesses faith, possesses shame and moral dread, is diligent, possesses mindfulness, possesses correct concentration and wisdom, is not sluggish, keeps his mind set on seclusion, deeply respects the precepts, is concerned with the conduct of a śramaṇa, aspires to nirvāṇa, and has gone forth for the sake of the Dharma—such a bhikṣu should be instructed. For what reason? Because such a bhikṣu is able to cultivate the holy life and is able to establish (pratiṣṭhā) himself.”
right: The Buddha said to Śāriputra: "If that monk is devious, deceitful, fraudulent, untrusting, lacking in shame (hrī) and lacking in remorse (apatrāpya), lazy, lacking in mindfulness (smṛti), lacking in stable wisdom (prajñā), sluggish, opposed to seclusion (viveka), disrespectful of the training rules (śikṣāpada), unmindful of the conduct of a renunciant (śramaṇa), and does not seek liberation (nirvāṇa), having gone forth for the sake of his livelihood, such a monk should not be instructed or spoken with. For what reason? Because such monks destroy the holy life (brahmacarya). If that monk is not devious, not deceitful, not fraudulent, is trusting, possesses shame and remorse, is diligent and mindful, possesses stable wisdom, is not sluggish, keeps his mind set on seclusion, deeply respects the training rules, is mindful of the conduct of a renunciant, aspires to liberation, and has gone forth for the sake of the Dharma, such a monk should be instructed. For what reason? Because such a monk is able to cultivate the holy life and is able to establish himself."

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 云何菩薩清淨靜慮？謂此靜慮略有十種。一者、由世間淨，離諸愛味清淨靜慮。二者、由出世淨，無有染污清淨靜慮。三者、由加行淨，清淨靜慮。四者、由得根本淨，清淨靜慮。五者、由根本勝進淨，清淨靜慮。六者、由入、住、出自在淨，清淨靜慮。七者、捨靜慮已，復還證入自在淨，清淨靜慮。八者、神通變現自在淨，清淨靜慮。九者、離一切見趣淨，清淨靜慮。十者、一切煩惱、所知障淨，清淨靜慮。
left: What is the pure meditative absorption (dhyāna) of a bodhisattva? In brief, this meditative absorption is of ten kinds. First, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the worldly (loka), being free from all craving for its flavor. Second, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the supramundane (lokottara), being without any defilement (kliṣṭa). Third, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the preparatory practice (prayoga). Fourth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of attaining the fundamental (mūla). Fifth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the superior progress from the fundamental. Sixth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of mastery in entering, abiding, and emerging. Seventh, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of mastery in abandoning the meditative absorption and then returning to realize and enter it again. Eighth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of mastery in the miraculous manifestation of supernormal powers (abhijñā). Ninth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of being free from all views (sarva-dṛṣṭi). Tenth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purification of all defilements (sarva-kleśa) and the obstruction to knowledge (jñāna-āvaraṇa-viśuddhi).
right: What is the pure meditative absorption (dhyāna) of a bodhisattva? In brief, this meditative absorption is of ten kinds. First, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of worldly purity, being free from all craving for its flavor. Second, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of supramundane purity, being without any defilement. Third, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of preparatory practice (prayoga). Fourth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of attaining the fundamental (maula). Fifth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of superior progress from the fundamental. Sixth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of mastery in entering, abiding, and emerging. Seventh, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of mastery in emerging from the meditative absorption and then returning to realize and enter it again. Eighth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity of mastery in the manifestation of supernormal powers (abhijñā). Ninth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of being free from all inclinations toward views (dṛṣṭi). Tenth, the pure meditative absorption that is pure by way of the purity from all afflictions (kleśa) and the obstructions to knowledge (jñeyāvaraṇa).

title: 瑜伽師地論
text: 復次，云何菩薩失壞大乘？謂有菩薩，聞一切法甚深無性，即執一切煩惱燒然自性本無，謂已無有生死重病。譬如有人，於己身中所生熱病，謂為無病，於此熱病不能解脫，名為失壞。由此譬喻，失壞菩薩，當知亦爾。
left: Furthermore, how does a bodhisattva (bodhisattva) lose the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna)? It is when a bodhisattva hears that all phenomena (dharma) are profound and lack intrinsic nature (niḥsvabhāva), and immediately clings to the view that all defilements (kleśa) are burning and inherently non-existent, believing that the grave sickness of birth-and-death (saṃsāra) no longer exists. It is like a person who, having a fever within their own body, claims to be free of sickness; because they cannot be liberated from this fever, it is called a loss. By this analogy, you should know that a bodhisattva who has suffered such a loss is the same.
right: Furthermore, how does a bodhisattva (bodhisattva) lose the Great Vehicle (mahāyāna)? It is when a bodhisattva hears that all phenomena (sarva-dharma) are profound and without intrinsic nature (niḥsvabhāva), and immediately clings to the view that the burning intrinsic nature of all defilements (sarva-kleśa) is originally non-existent, claiming that the grave sickness of transmigration (saṃsāra) no longer exists. It is like a person who, having a fever within their own body (kāya), claims to be without sickness; because they cannot be liberated (vimukti) from this fever, it is called a loss. By this analogy, one should know that the bodhisattva who has suffered a loss is likewise.

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：善無漏法亦名為妙。諸染污法亦名有罪有覆及劣。准此妙劣，餘中已成，故頌不辯。諸有為善亦名應習，餘非應習義准已成。何故無為不名應習？不可數習令增長故。又習為果，此無果故。解脫涅槃亦名無上，以無一法能勝涅槃，是善是常超眾法故。餘法有上，義准已成。
left: The treatise says: Virtuous (kuśala) undefiled (anāsrava) phenomena (dharma) are also called excellent (praṇīta). All defiled (saṃkliṣṭa) phenomena are also called faulty (sāvādya), obstructive (āvṛta), and inferior (hīna). Based on these categories of excellent and inferior, the status of the remainder is already established by implication, and therefore the verse does not discuss it. All conditioned (saṃskṛta) virtuous phenomena are also called worthy of cultivation (bhāvanīya), and the fact that others are not worthy of cultivation is established by implication. Why is the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) not called worthy of cultivation? Because it cannot be repeatedly cultivated to cause it to increase. Furthermore, cultivation has a result, and this has no result. Liberation (vimukti) and Nirvana (nirvāṇa) are also called supreme (anuttara), because there is no phenomenon that can surpass Nirvana, as it is virtuous, eternal (nitya), and transcends all phenomena. That other phenomena have something superior to them is established by implication.
right: The treatise says: Virtuous undefiled phenomena (anāsrava-dharma) are also called excellent (anuttara). All defiled phenomena (kliṣṭa) are also called faulty, covered, and inferior. Based on these categories of excellent and inferior, the status of the remainder is already established by implication, and therefore the verse does not discuss it. All virtuous conditioned phenomena (saṃskṛta) are also called worthy of cultivation; the remainder is not worthy of cultivation, which is established by implication. Why is the unconditioned (asaṃskṛta) not called worthy of cultivation? Because it cannot be repeatedly cultivated to cause growth. Furthermore, cultivation has a result, and this has no result. Liberation (vimukti) and Nirvana (nirvāṇa) are also called supreme (anuttara), because there is not one phenomenon that can surpass Nirvana, as it is virtuous, eternal, and transcends all phenomena. The remainder of phenomena have something superior to them, which is established by implication.

title: 雜阿含經
text: 長者答言：「我之所見真實、有為、思量、緣起，若復真實、有為、思量、緣起者，彼則無常，無常者是苦。如是知已，於一切見都無所得。如汝所見：『世間常，此是真實，餘則虛妄。』者，此見真實、有為、思量、緣起；若真實、有為、思量、緣起者，是則無常，無常者是苦。是故汝等習近於苦，唯得於苦，堅住於苦，深入於苦。如是汝言世間無常，此是真實，餘則虛妄。有如是咎。」
left: The householder (gṛhapati) replied: “What I see is real (satya), conditioned (saṃskṛta), thought-constructed (cintā), and dependent-arising (pratītyasamutpāda). If it is real, conditioned, thought-constructed, and dependent-arising, then it is impermanent (anitya). What is impermanent is suffering (duḥkha). Having known it in this way, one attains no-apprehension (anupalambha) regarding all views (dṛṣṭi). As for your view that ‘the world (loka) is permanent, this is real, and the rest is false,’ this view is real, conditioned, thought-constructed, and dependent-arising. If it is real, conditioned, thought-constructed, and dependent-arising, then it is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. Therefore, you all associate with suffering, obtain only suffering, remain firmly in suffering, and sink deeply into suffering. In the same way, when you say ‘the world is impermanent, this is real, and the rest is false,’ there is this same fault.”
right: The elder replied: "What I see is real (satya), conditioned (saṃskṛta), thought-out (cintāmaya), and dependent-arising (pratītyasamutpanna). If it is real, conditioned, thought-out, and dependent-arising, then it is impermanent (anitya). What is impermanent is suffering (duḥkha). Having known this, one finds nothing to grasp in all views. As for your view that 'The world is eternal, this is real, and all else is false,' this view is real, conditioned, thought-out, and dependent-arising. If it is real, conditioned, thought-out, and dependent-arising, then it is impermanent. What is impermanent is suffering. Therefore, you all associate with suffering, obtain only suffering, remain firmly in suffering, and sink deep into suffering. Thus, when you say 'The world is impermanent, this is real, and all else is false,' you have such a fault."

title: 雜阿含經
text: 佛告婆羅門出家：「有三種婆羅門真實，我自覺悟成等正覺而復為人演說。汝婆羅門出家作如是說：『不害一切眾生，是婆羅門真諦，非為虛妄。』彼於彼言我勝、言相似、言我卑，若於彼真諦不繫著，於一切世間作慈心色像，是名第一婆羅門真諦，我自覺悟成等正覺，為人演說。
left: The Buddha said to the brahmin (brāhmaṇa) who had gone forth (pravrajita): “There are three kinds of true brahmins, which I have realized for myself (pratyātma) and attained complete perfect awakening (abhisaṃbodhi), and which I now explain to others. You, brahmin who has gone forth, speak thus: ‘Not harming any living being (sarva-sattva) is the true reality of a brahmin, and it is not false.’ If one does not cling to that true reality—whether one says of others that ‘I am superior,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’—and if one maintains a disposition of loving-kindness (maitra-citta) toward all the world (sarva-loka), this is called the first true reality of a brahmin, which I have realized for myself and attained complete perfect awakening, and which I explain to others.”
right: The Buddha said to the brahmin who had gone forth: “There are three kinds of brahmin truths that I have awakened to by myself, attained complete and perfect awakening (samyaksambodhi), and then explained to others. You, brahmin who have gone forth, speak thus: ‘Not harming any living being is the true reality (satya) of a brahmin, and it is not false.’ If one does not cling to that truth by saying ‘I am superior,’ ‘I am equal,’ or ‘I am inferior’ in relation to others, but instead manifests a mind of loving-kindness (maitrī) toward the entire world, this is called the first brahmin truth, which I have awakened to by myself, attained complete and perfect awakening, and explained to others.”

title: 雜阿含經
text: 「若正說佛子從佛口生，從法化生，得佛法分者，則我身是也。所以者何？我是佛子，從佛口生，從法化生，得佛法分，以少方便，得禪、解脫、三昧、正受。譬如轉輪聖王長太子，雖未灌頂，已得王法，不勤方便，能得五欲功德。我亦如是，為佛之子，不勤方便，得禪、解脫、三昧、正受，於一日中，世尊以神通力三至我所，三教授我，以大人處所建立於我。」
left: "If one were to speak correctly, saying that a son of the Buddha (buddha-putra) is born from the mouth of the Buddha, born through transformation by the Dharma (dharma), and obtains a portion of the Buddha-Dharma, then I am that person. Why is this? I am a son of the Buddha, born from the mouth of the Buddha, born through transformation by the Dharma, and have obtained a portion of the Buddha-Dharma, having attained through little effort the meditative absorption (dhyāna), liberation (vimokṣa), concentration (samādhi), and correct reception (samāpatti). It is like the eldest prince (kumāra) of a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin), who, although not yet anointed, already possesses the royal law and, without strenuous effort, is able to obtain the merits (guṇa) of the five desires. I am also like this; being a son of the Buddha, without strenuous effort, I have attained meditative absorption, liberation, concentration, and correct reception. In a single day, the Blessed One (bhagavant) came to me three times through his power of supernormal knowledge (abhijñā), instructed me three times, and established me in the place of a great man."
right: "If one were to speak correctly of a son of the Buddha (buddhaputra) as born from the Buddha’s mouth, born through transformation by the Dharma (dharma), and having obtained a portion of the Buddha-Dharma, then that person is myself. Why is this? I am a son of the Buddha, born from the Buddha’s mouth, born through transformation by the Dharma, and having obtained a portion of the Buddha-Dharma; with little effort, I have attained meditative absorption (dhyāna), liberation (vimokṣa), concentration (samādhi), and correct reception (samāpatti). It is like the eldest son of a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin): although he has not yet been anointed, he already possesses the royal law and, without strenuous effort, is able to obtain the merits of the five desires. I am also like this; as a son of the Buddha, without strenuous effort, I have attained meditative absorption, liberation, concentration, and correct reception. Within a single day, the World-Honored One (bhagavat) came to me three times through his supernatural power (ṛddhi), instructed me three times, and established me in the station of a great man."

title: 雜阿含經
text: 「聚落主！何等為三種卑下、田舍、常人凡夫樂受欲樂？有受欲者，非法濫取，不以安樂自供，不供養父母、給足兄弟、妻子、奴婢、眷屬、朋友、知識，亦不隨時供養沙門、婆羅門、仰求勝處安樂果報、未來生天，是名世間第一受欲。
left: "Village headman! What are the three kinds of base, rustic, and common worldling (pṛthagjana) enjoyments of sensual pleasure? There is one who enjoys sensual pleasure, who acquires it through unrighteousness (adharma), who does not provide for his own happiness, who does not make offerings (pūjā) to his parents, nor provide for his brothers, wife, children, servants, attendants, friends, or acquaintances, and who also does not at the proper time make offerings to renunciants (śramaṇa) or brāhmaṇas (brāhmaṇa), nor seek the fruit of happiness (phala-vipāka) in higher realms or future rebirth in heaven; this is called the first worldly (laukika-agra) enjoyment of sensual pleasure."
right: "Village headman! What are the three kinds of base, rustic, and common worldly pleasures of sense-desire (kāma)? There is one who, while experiencing sense-desires, acquires them through unlawful means, does not provide for his own comfort, does not support his parents, provide for his brothers, wife, servants, dependents, friends, or acquaintances, and does not at the proper time make offerings to renunciants (śramaṇa) and brāhmaṇas (brāhmaṇa) while seeking the fruit of happiness in a superior realm or a future birth in heaven; this is called the first worldly pleasure of sense-desire."

title: 雜阿含經
text: 須臾默然思惟已，語尊者那伽達多言：「青者謂戒也，白覆謂解脫也，一輻者身念也，轉者轉出也，車者止觀也，離結者有三種結，謂貪、恚、癡。彼阿羅漢諸漏已盡、已滅、已知、已斷根本，如截多羅樹頭更不復生，未來世滅不起法。
left: After remaining silent for a moment in contemplation, he said to the Venerable Nāgadatta: "The blue refers to moral discipline (śīla), the white covering refers to liberation (vimukti), the single spoke refers to mindfulness of the body (kāyagatāsati), the turning refers to turning away, and the chariot refers to serenity and insight (śamathavipaśyanā). As for being free from fetters (saṃyojana), there are three kinds of fetters: greed (lobha), hatred (dveṣa), and delusion (moha). That arhat has exhausted all influxes (āsrava), they are extinguished, known, and their roots have been cut off, just like cutting off the crown of a Palmyra tree so that it will not grow again, a phenomenon that is extinguished and will not arise in the future."
right: After remaining silent for a moment in contemplation, he said to the venerable (sthavira) Nāgadatta: "The blue refers to moral discipline (śīla), the white covering refers to liberation (vimokṣa), the single spoke refers to mindfulness of the body (kāya-smṛti), the turning refers to turning away, and the chariot refers to serenity and insight (śamatha-vipaśyanā). Being free from fetters (saṃyojana) refers to the three kinds of fetters, namely greed, hatred, and delusion. That worthy one (arhant) has exhausted all influxes (āsrava), they are extinguished, known, and their root is cut off, like cutting off the crown of a Palmyra tree so that it will not grow again, a phenomenon that is extinguished and does not arise in the future (anāgata-adhvan)."

title: 雜阿含經
text: 「若於此五恐怖罪怨對休息、於三法決定離疑惑、於聖意如實知見，是聖弟子能自記說：『我地獄盡，畜生、餓鬼惡趣盡，得須陀洹，不墮惡趣法，決定正趣三菩提，七有天人往生，究竟苦邊。』」
left: “If one has ceased from these five terrifying acts of enmity, is firmly free from doubt regarding the three teachings (tri-dharma), and truly sees and knows the noble intent (ārya-abhiprāya), this noble disciple (ārya-śrāvaka) is able to declare of himself: ‘My hell is ended; the animal realm and the hungry ghost realm—the evil destinies (durgati)—are ended. I have attained the stream-enterer (srotāpanna), I am not subject to falling into an evil destiny, I am firmly destined for full awakening (sambodhi), and after at most seven existences of being reborn among gods and humans, I will reach the complete ending of suffering (duḥkha).’”
right: “If one has ceased from these five terrifying sins and enmities, is firmly free from doubt regarding the three truths, and possesses knowledge and vision (jñāna-darśana) of the noble intent as it really is (yathābhūtam), that noble disciple (ārya-śrāvaka) is able to declare of himself: ‘My hell is ended; the animal realm and the hungry ghost realm—the evil destinies (apāya)—are ended. I have attained the stream-enterer (srotaāpanna) state, I am not subject to the law of falling into evil destinies, I am firmly destined for full awakening (sambodhi), I will wander for at most seven existences among gods and humans (deva-manuṣya), and I will reach the complete ending (niṣṭhā) of suffering.’”

title: 成唯識論
text: 云何漸次悟入唯識？謂諸菩薩於識相、性，資糧位中能深信解；在加行位能漸伏除所取、能取，引發真見；在通達位如實通達；修習位中如所見理，數數修習伏斷餘障；至究竟位出障圓明，能盡未來化有情類，復令悟入唯識相、性。
left: How does one gradually awaken to and enter into Consciousness-Only (vijñaptimātra)? It is said that Bodhisattvas, while in the stage of provisioning (saṃbhāra-mārga), are able to deeply believe in and understand the characteristics (lakṣaṇa) and nature (svabhāva) of consciousness. In the stage of applied effort (prayoga-mārga), they are able to gradually subdue and eliminate the grasped (grāhya) and the grasper (grāhaka), thereby inducing true vision. In the stage of realization (prativedha-mārga), they realize these as they truly are. In the stage of cultivation (bhāvanā-mārga), they repeatedly practice in accordance with the principles they have perceived, in order to subdue and sever the remaining hindrances (āvaraṇa). Upon arriving at the ultimate stage (niṣṭhā-mārga), they emerge from all hindrances with perfect clarity, able to transform all classes of sentient beings until the end of time, and further cause them to awaken to and enter into the characteristics and nature of Consciousness-Only.
right: How does one gradually awaken to and enter Consciousness-Only (vijñapti-mātra)? It means that Bodhisattvas, during the stage of provisioning (sambhāra), are able to deeply believe in and understand the characteristics (lakṣaṇa) and nature (svabhāva) of consciousness; during the stage of applied effort (prayoga), they are able to gradually subdue and eliminate the grasped (grāhya) and the grasper (grāhaka) to induce true vision (darśana); during the stage of realization (pratipatti), they realize these as they truly are (yathābhūtam); during the stage of cultivation (bhāvanā), they repeatedly practice in accordance with the principles they have perceived to subdue and sever the remaining hindrances; and upon arriving at the ultimate stage (niṣṭhā), they emerge from obstacles with perfect clarity, able to transform all classes of sentient beings (sattva-nikāya) until the end of time (anāgata), and cause them to awaken to and enter the characteristics and nature of Consciousness-Only.

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：由田勝者，聞有苾芻於僧眾中作女人語，彼於現世轉作女人。此等傳聞其類非一。由意勝者，聞有黃門救脫諸牛黃門事故，彼於現世轉作丈夫。此等傳聞事亦非一。或生此地永離此地染，於此地中諸善不善業。於異熟定位不定者，此業必能招現法果。若有餘位順定受業，彼必定無永離染義，必於餘位受異熟果。若於異熟亦不定者，永離染故不受異熟。何田起業定即受耶？頌曰：
left:
The treatise says: Regarding those superior in terms of the field, it is heard that a bhikṣu (monk) spoke to the community of monks using the speech of a woman, and in this very lifetime he was transformed into a woman. Such reports are not singular. Regarding those superior in terms of intention, it is heard that a eunuch (paṇḍaka) saved some cattle from a eunuch-related incident, and in this very lifetime he was transformed into a man (puruṣa). Such reports are also not singular.

As for wholesome and unwholesome karman (action) performed in this state, if one is born into this state and permanently detaches from the defilements (vairāgya) of this state, then for that karman which is uncertain regarding the timing of its ripening (vipāka), that karman will inevitably bring about a result in the present lifetime (dṛṣṭadharma). If there is other karman that is certain to be experienced in a subsequent state, then for that person there is no meaning in having permanently detached from defilements, for they will certainly experience the ripening in a subsequent state. If the ripening itself is also uncertain, then because one has permanently detached from defilements, one will not experience the ripening.

What is the field from which karman arises such that it is certain to be experienced? The gāthā (verse) says:
right:
The treatise says: Regarding the excellence of the field, it is heard that there was a monk (bhikṣu) who spoke like a woman in the midst of the monastic community, and because of that, he was transformed into a woman in his present lifetime. Such reports are not singular. Regarding the excellence of intention, it is heard that there was a eunuch (paṇḍaka) who saved cows from the affairs of eunuchs, and because of that, he was transformed into a man in his present lifetime. Such reports are also not singular.

Or, one may be born in this realm and permanently abandon the defilements (kleśa) of this realm, regarding the wholesome and unwholesome actions (karman) within this realm. For an action that is certain in its ripening (vipāka) but uncertain in its timing, this action will inevitably bring about a result in the present lifetime. If there is an action that is certain to be experienced in another lifetime, it certainly lacks the meaning of having permanently abandoned defilements, and it will necessarily experience its ripening in another lifetime. If the ripening itself is also uncertain, then because one has permanently abandoned defilements, one will not experience the ripening. From what field does an action arise such that it is certain to be experienced? The verse says:

title: 成唯識論
text: 是出世間無分別智，斷世間故，名「出世間」。二取隨眠是世間本，唯此能斷獨得「出」名。或「出世」名依二義立，謂體無漏及證真如，此智具斯二種義故，獨名「出世」，餘智不然，即十地中無分別智。
left: This is supramundane (lokottara) non-conceptual wisdom (nirvikalpa-jñāna); it is called "supramundane" because it severs the mundane (loka). The latencies (anuśaya) of the twofold grasping are the root of the mundane, and because only this wisdom can sever them, it alone receives the name "supramundane." Alternatively, the name "supramundane" is established based on two meanings (artha): its essence is untainted (anāsrava), and it realizes True Suchness (tathatā). Because this wisdom possesses these two kinds (dvividha) of meanings, it alone is called "supramundane," whereas other forms of wisdom are not; this refers to the non-conceptual wisdom within the ten stages (daśan-bhūmi).
right: This is supramundane non-conceptual wisdom (nirvikalpa-jñāna); it is called "supramundane" (lokottara) because it severs the mundane. The latencies (anuśaya) of the twofold grasping are the root of the mundane, and because only this wisdom can sever them, it alone receives the name "supramundane." Alternatively, the name "supramundane" is established based on two meanings: its essence is untainted (anāsrava), and it realizes True Suchness (tathatā). Because this wisdom possesses these two meanings, it alone is called "supramundane," whereas other forms of wisdom are not; this refers to the non-conceptual wisdom within the ten stages (daśabhūmi).

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：無從果退中間命終，退已須臾必還得故。如契經說：苾芻當知，如是多聞諸聖弟子退失正念，速復還能令所退起盡沒滅離。若謂不然，修梵行果應非安隱可委信處。又住果位所不應為違果事業，由慚增故於暫退時亦必不造，譬如壯士雖蹶不仆。如上所言，有練根得無學有學，正練根時各幾無間、幾解脫道？何性攝？何所依？頌曰：
left: The Commentary says: There is no death in the interval of having fallen from the fruit (phala), because once fallen, one must surely regain it in a mere moment. As the Discourses (sūtra) say: "Bhikṣus, you should know that if such a learned noble disciple loses right mindfulness (smṛti), he is able to quickly return and cause that which arose from the fall to be exhausted, extinguished, and abandoned." If this were not so, the fruit of practicing the holy life (brahmacarya) would not be a secure place to be trusted. Furthermore, one who abides in the state of the fruit does not perform actions contrary to that fruit; because their shame (hrī) has increased, they do not commit such acts even when temporarily fallen, just as a strong man, though he stumbles, does not fall. As stated above, there are those who, by refining their faculties (indriya), attain the state of one beyond training (aśaikṣa) or one in training (śaikṣa). When they are in the process of refining their faculties, how many paths of immediate succession (ānantarya-mārga) and how many paths of liberation (vimukti-mārga) are there for each? What nature (svabhāva) are they included in? What is their basis (āśraya)? The Verse says:
right:
The Commentary says: There is no death in the interval for one who has fallen from the fruit, because once fallen, one must surely regain it in a mere moment. As the Sūtra (sūtra) says: "Bhikṣus (bhikṣu), you should know that if such a learned (bahu-śruta) noble disciple (ārya-śrāvaka) loses right mindfulness (samyak smṛti), he is able to quickly return and cause that which arose from the fall to be exhausted, extinguished, and abandoned." If this were not so, the fruit of practicing the holy life (brahmacarya) would not be a secure place to be trusted. Furthermore, one who abides in the stage of the fruit does not perform actions (karman) that are contrary to that fruit; because their sense of shame has increased, they do not commit such acts even when temporarily fallen, just as a strong man, though he stumbles, does not fall. As stated above, there are those who, by refining their faculties, attain the state of one beyond training (aśaikṣa) or one in training (śaikṣa). When refining the faculties, how many paths of immediate result (ānantarya-mārga) and how many paths of liberation (vimukti-mārga) are there for each? What is their nature (svabhāva) included in? What is their basis (āśraya)? The Verse says:

None who fall from the fruit will die before they have surely regained it;
They do not perform what is not done while abiding in the fruit,
For their shame has increased and thus they do not act so.

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：經說通行總有四種：一苦遲通行、二苦速通行、三樂遲通行、四樂速通行。道依根本四靜慮生名樂通行，以攝受支止觀平等任運轉故。道依無色、未至、中間名苦通行，以不攝支止觀不等艱辛轉故。謂無色定觀減止增，未至、中間觀增止減。即此樂苦二通行中，鈍根名遲、利根名速。二行於境通達稽遲故名遲通，翻此名速。或遲鈍者所起通行名遲通行，速此相違。道亦名為菩提分法。此有幾種？名義云何？頌曰：
left:
The treatise says: The sutras state that there are four kinds of routes (pratipad): first, the difficult route with slow realization (duḥkhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā); second, the difficult route with quick realization (duḥkhā pratipad kṣiprābhijñā); third, the easy route with slow realization (sukhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā); and fourth, the easy route with quick realization (sukhā pratipad kṣiprābhijñā).

A path arising in reliance on the four fundamental meditative absorptions (dhyāna) is called an "easy route," because it incorporates the factors of the absorption, and because tranquility (śamatha) and insight (vipaśyanā) are balanced, allowing it to proceed effortlessly. A path relying on the formless attainments (ārūpya), the threshold state (anāgamya), or the intermediate absorption (dhyānāntara) is called a "difficult route," because it does not incorporate those factors, and because tranquility and insight are unequal, causing it to proceed with hardship. Specifically, in the formless attainments, insight is diminished and tranquility is increased, while in the threshold state and the intermediate absorption, insight is increased and tranquility is diminished.

Within these two modes of progress, the pleasant and the painful, those with dull faculties (mṛdvindriya) are termed "slow," while those with sharp faculties (tīkṣṇendriya) are termed "quick." Because the two modes of progress reach their object with delay, they are called "slow," and the opposite of this is called "quick." Alternatively, the progress undertaken by one who is dull-witted is called "slow progress," and "quick" is the opposite of this. The path is also called the factors of awakening (bodhipākṣika-dharma). How many kinds are there? What are their names and meanings? The verse says:
right: The treatise says: The scriptures state that there are four kinds of modes of progress (pratipad): first, the painful mode with slow realization; second, the painful mode with quick realization; third, the pleasant mode with slow realization; and fourth, the pleasant mode with quick realization. A path arising in reliance on the four fundamental meditative absorptions (catur-dhyāna) is called a "pleasant mode of progress," because it incorporates the factors of absorption and because tranquility (śamatha) and insight (vipaśyanā) are balanced, allowing it to proceed effortlessly. A path relying on the formless absorptions (ārūpya-samāpatti), the threshold state, or the intermediate state is called a "painful mode of progress," because it does not incorporate those factors, and because tranquility and insight are unequal, causing it to proceed with hardship. Specifically, in the formless absorptions, insight is diminished and tranquility is increased, whereas in the threshold and intermediate states, insight is increased and tranquility is diminished. Within these two modes of progress, the pleasant and the painful, those with dull faculties are termed "slow," while those with sharp faculties are termed "quick." Because these two modes of progress are slow in realizing their objects, they are called "slow progress," and the opposite of this is called "quick." Alternatively, the progress undertaken by one who is dull-witted is called "slow progress," and "quick" is the opposite of this. The path is also called the factors of awakening (bodhi-pakṣya). How many kinds of these are there, and what is the meaning of their names? The verse says:

title: 成唯識論
text: 汝應諦聽：若唯一識，寧有十方凡聖、尊卑、因果等別？誰為誰說？何法何求？故「唯識」言有深意趣。「識」言總顯一切有情各有八識、六位心所，所變相、見、分位差別及彼空理所顯真如。識自相故，識相應故，二所變故，三分位故，四實性故，如是諸法皆不離識，總立識名。「唯」言，但遮愚夫所執定離諸識實有色等。
left: You should listen well: if there were only a single consciousness, how could there be distinctions such as the ten directions (daśan-diś), the ordinary and the sacred, the venerable and the base, or cause and effect (hetu-phala)? Who would preach to whom? What dharma would be sought? Therefore, the term "consciousness-only" has a profound intent. The word "consciousness" (vijñāna) collectively reveals that all sentient beings (sarva-sattva) each possess eight consciousnesses and six categories of mental associates, the distinctions in the states (avasthā-bheda) of the transformed "seen" and "seeing" parts, as well as the True Suchness (tathatā) revealed by the principle of emptiness. Because of the self-nature (sva-lakṣaṇa) of consciousness, because of the association of consciousness (vijñāna-saṃprayuj), because of the two types of transformation, because of the three types of states, and because of the four types of ultimate reality, all such dharmas (sarva-dharma) are not separate from consciousness, and are thus collectively given the name "consciousness." The word "only" simply excludes the real existence of form (rūpa) and other phenomena that the ignorant (bāla) cling to as being definitely separate from the various consciousnesses.
right: You should listen attentively: if there were only a single consciousness (vijñapti), how could there be distinctions such as the ten directions, the ordinary and the sacred, the venerable and the base, or cause and effect? Who would preach to whom? What dharma would be sought? Therefore, the term "consciousness-only" (vijñaptimātra) has a profound intent. The word "consciousness" collectively reveals that all sentient beings each possess eight consciousnesses (vijñāna) and six categories of mental associates (caitta), the distinctions in the states of the "seen" (nimitta-bhāga) and "seeing" (darśana-bhāga) parts transformed from them, as well as the True Suchness (tathatā) revealed by the principle of emptiness (śūnyatā). Because of the self-nature of consciousness, because of the association of consciousness, because of the two transformations, because of the three states, and because of the four real natures, all such phenomena (dharma) are not separate from consciousness, and are thus collectively given the name "consciousness." The word "only" (mātra) simply excludes the real existence of form and other phenomena that the ignorant cling to as being definitely separate from the various consciousnesses.

title: 成唯識論
text: 《瑜伽論》說：若任運生一切煩惱，皆於三受現行可得。若通一切識身者，遍與一切根相應；不通一切識身者，意地一切根相應。《雜集論》說：若欲界繫任運煩惱，發惡行者，亦是不善。所餘皆是有覆無記。
left: The Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra states: If all afflictions (kleśa) arise spontaneously (sahaja), they can all be found manifesting in connection with the three feelings (vedanā). If they are common to all groups of consciousness (vijñāna-kāya), they are universally associated with all faculties (indriya); if they are not common to all groups of consciousness, they are associated with all faculties in the mental ground (manobhūmi). The Abhidharmasamuccaya states: If spontaneous afflictions bound to the desire realm (kāmadhātu) produce evil conduct (akuśala-karman), they are also unwholesome (akuśala); all others are obscured and indeterminate (nivṛtāvyākṛta).
right: The Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra states: if all afflictions (kleśa) arise spontaneously, they can all be found manifesting in connection with the three feelings (vedanā). If they are common to all groups of consciousness (vijñāna-kāya), they are universally associated with all faculties (indriya); if they are not common to all groups of consciousness, they are associated with all faculties in the mental ground (manobhūmi). The Abhidharmasamuccaya states: if spontaneous afflictions bound to the desire realm (kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyuj) produce evil conduct, they are also unwholesome (akuśala); all others are obscured and indeterminate (nivṛta-avyākṛta).

title: 成唯識論
text: 前、中、後際，生死輪迴，不待外緣，既由內識，淨法相續，應知亦然。謂無始來，依附本識，有、無漏種，由轉識等，數數熏發，漸漸增勝，乃至究竟，得成佛時，轉捨本來雜染識種，轉得始起清淨種識，任持一切功德種子。由本願力，盡未來際，起諸妙用，相續無窮。
left: Regarding the past, present, and future (apara-anta), the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra) does not depend on external conditions; since it arises from internal consciousness, the continuity (saṃtāna) of pure phenomena should be understood in the same way. It is said that from beginningless time, there have adhered to the fundamental consciousness both tainted and untainted seeds (bīja), which, through the transforming consciousness and so forth, are repeatedly perfumed and stimulated, gradually increasing in strength until the ultimate (niṣṭhā) attainment of Buddhahood. At that time, one transforms and abandons the originally defiled consciousness-seeds and transforms and attains the newly arisen pure consciousness-seeds, which sustain the seeds of all virtues (sarva-guṇa). By the power of the original vows (praṇidhāna-bala), until the end of future time (aparānta-koṭi), various marvelous functions arise in an endless succession.
right: Regarding the past, present, and future, the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra) does not depend on external conditions; since it arises from internal consciousness (vijñāna), the continuity of pure phenomena (dharma) should be understood in the same way. From beginningless time, there have adhered to the fundamental consciousness (mūlavijñāna) both tainted and untainted seeds (bīja). Through the transforming consciousnesses (pravṛttivijñāna) and others, these are repeatedly perfumed and activated, gradually increasing in strength until, at the point of ultimate attainment—when one becomes a Buddha—one abandons the originally defiled seeds of consciousness and transforms them to obtain the newly arisen pure seeds of consciousness, which sustain all seeds of merit (guṇa). By the power of original vows (pūrva-praṇidhāna), various marvelous functions arise until the end of future time in an endless succession.

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：諸靜慮地所繫善法，由二緣捨：一由易地，謂從下地生上地時，或上地沒來生下地；二由得退，謂從已獲勝定功德還退失時。等言為顯捨眾同分亦捨少分殊勝善根，如色界中所有善法由易地退捨，無色界亦然，唯無律儀與色界異。無漏善法由三緣捨：一由得果，謂得果時捨前向道及果道故；二由練根，謂練根位由得利道捨鈍道故；三由退失，謂得退時退失果道勝果道故。如是已說捨諸律儀。不律儀云何捨？頌曰：
left:
The treatise says: The wholesome dharmas (kuśala-dharma) bound to the stages of meditative concentration (dhyāna-bhūmi) are abandoned for two reasons: first, by changing planes (bhūmi-saṃkrama), which means when one is born from a lower plane into a higher plane, or when one passes away from a higher plane and is reborn in a lower plane; second, by falling away (parihāṇi), which means when one falls away from the merits of a superior concentration (dhyāna-guṇa) that one has already attained. The word "etc." is used to indicate that one also abandons the shared characteristics (nikāya-sabhāga) and certain specific superior wholesome roots (kuśala-mūla). Just as all wholesome dharmas in the form realm (rūpa-dhātu) are abandoned through changing planes or falling away, the same is true for the formless realm (ārūpya-dhātu), except that there is no discipline (saṃvara) there, which differs from the form realm.

Wholesome dharmas that are undefiled (anāsrava-dharma) are abandoned for three reasons: first, by attaining a fruit (phala-prāpti), meaning that when one attains a fruit, one abandons the preceding path of the candidate (pratipannaka-mārga) and the path of the previous fruit; second, by refining the faculties (indriya-saṃśodhana), meaning that at the stage of refining the faculties, one abandons the dull path (mṛdv-indriya-mārga) by obtaining the sharp path (tīkṣṇ-indriya-mārga); third, by falling away, meaning that when one experiences a falling away, one loses the path of the fruit or the path of a superior fruit.

Thus, the abandonment of the various disciplines has been explained. How is non-discipline (asaṃvara) abandoned? The stanza says:
right:

The word "etc." is used to indicate that one also abandons the shared group (nikāya-sabhāga) and abandons a small portion of superior wholesome roots (kuśala-mūla). Just as all wholesome dharmas in the form realm (rūpadhātu) are abandoned through changing planes or falling away, the formless realm (ārūpya-dhātu) is the same, except that it lacks discipline (saṃvara), which differs from the form realm.

Wholesome dharmas that are undefiled (anāsrava) are abandoned for three reasons: first, by attaining a fruit, which means that at the time of attaining a fruit, one abandons the preceding path of the candidate and the path of the previous fruit; second, by refining the faculties, which means that at the stage of refining the faculties, one abandons the dull path by obtaining the sharp path; third, by falling away, which means that when one experiences a falling away, one loses the path of the fruit or the path of a superior fruit.

Thus, the abandonment of all discipline has been explained. How is non-discipline (asaṃvara) abandoned? The stanza says:

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：若住律儀，由勝煩惱作殺縛等諸不善業，由此便發不善無表；住不律儀，由淳淨信作禮佛等諸勝善業，由此亦發諸善無表。乃至此二心未斷來，所發無表恒時相續，然其初念唯成現在，自茲以後通成過現。已辯無表，成表云何？頌曰：
left: The treatise says: If one who dwells in discipline (saṃvara) performs unwholesome actions (akuśala-karman) such as killing or binding due to powerful defilements (kleśa), they consequently produce unwholesome non-informative matter (avijñapti). If one who dwells in indiscipline (asaṃvara) performs superior wholesome actions (kuśala-karman) such as bowing to the Buddha due to pure faith (prasāda), they consequently also produce wholesome non-informative matter. Until these two types of mind are severed, the non-informative matter that is produced continues constantly (saṃtāna); however, its first moment exists only in the present (vartamāna), while from that point onward it exists in both the past and the present. Having already explained non-informative matter, how is informative matter accomplished? The verse says:
right: The treatise says: If one who dwells in discipline (saṃvara) performs unwholesome actions (akuśala-karman) such as killing or binding due to powerful defilements (kleśa), they consequently produce unwholesome non-informative matter (avijñapti); if one who dwells in indiscipline (asaṃvara) performs superior wholesome actions such as bowing to the Buddha due to pure faith (śraddhā), they consequently produce wholesome non-informative matter. As long as these two types of mind are not severed, the non-informative matter produced continues uninterruptedly; however, its first moment exists only in the present, while from that point onward it exists in both the past and the present. Having explained non-informative matter, how is informative matter (vijñapti) accomplished? The verse says:

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：如是五種設是異生，但施亦能招無量果。住最後有，名最後生。法師四田中，是何田所攝？是恩田攝。所以者何？為諸世間大善友故、無明所盲者能施慧眼故、開示世間安危事故、令有情生起無漏法身故。以要說者，善說法師乃至能為佛所作事故，於彼行施便招無量果。欲知諸業輕重相者，應知輕重略由六因。其六者何？頌曰：
left: The treatise says: Even if these five types are ordinary beings (pṛthagjana), giving to them can still bring about immeasurable fruit. Those who dwell in their final existence (caramabhava) are called those in their final birth. Among the four fields of merit (puṇyakṣetra), which field does the teacher of the Dharma (dharmabhāṇaka) belong to? He is included in the field of gratitude (kṛtajñakṣetra). Why is this? Because he is a great virtuous friend (kalyāṇamitra) to all the world, because he bestows the eye of wisdom (prajñācakṣus) upon those blinded by ignorance (avidyā), because he reveals the matters of safety and peril in the world, and because he enables sentient beings to give rise to the untainted Dharma-body (anāsravadharmakāya). In short, because a teacher who speaks well is even able to perform the work of a Buddha, giving to him brings about immeasurable fruit. If one wishes to know the characteristics of the lightness and heaviness of all actions (karman), one should know that lightness and heaviness are determined by six causes. What are the six? The verse says:
right: The treatise says: Even if these five kinds of beings are ordinary persons (pṛthagjana), giving to them can still bring about immeasurable fruit. One who dwells in their final existence (caramabhavika) is called one who has reached their final birth (caramabhavika). Because he is a great virtuous friend to all the world, because he can bestow the eye of wisdom upon those blinded by ignorance (avidyā), because he reveals the matters of safety and peril in the world (loka), and because he enables sentient beings (sattva) to give rise to the untainted (anāsrava) Dharma-body (dharmakāya). In short, because a skilled Dharma-preacher can even perform the work (kṛtya) of a Buddha, giving to him brings about immeasurable fruit. If one wishes to know the characteristics of the lightness or heaviness of various actions (karman), one should know that lightness and heaviness are briefly due to six causes. What are those six?
