title: 成唯識論
text: 復有二種：謂利自、他所修勝行，隨意樂力一切皆通自他利行，依別相說，六到彼岸、菩提分等，自利行攝；四種攝事、四無量等，一切皆是利他行攝。如是等行差別無邊，皆是此中所修勝行。
left: Furthermore, there are two kinds: namely, the superior practices (viśeṣacaryā) cultivated for the benefit of self and others. Through the power of one’s intention (āśaya), all practices are generally understood as benefiting both self and others. Speaking in terms of their distinct characteristics, the six perfections (pāramitā), the aids to enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma), and so forth are categorized as practices for self-benefit (svārthacaryā); the four means of attraction (saṃgrahavastu), the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), and so forth are all categorized as practices for the benefit of others (parārthacaryā). Such diverse practices are boundless, and all are the superior practices cultivated in this context.
right: Furthermore, there are two kinds: namely, the superior practices (viśeṣa-caryā) cultivated for the benefit of oneself and others. Through the power of intention (āśaya), all practices are generally capable of benefiting both oneself and others; however, speaking in terms of their distinct characteristics, the six perfections (pāramitā), the aids to enlightenment (bodhi-pakṣya), and so forth are categorized as practices for self-benefit (sva-artha), while the four means of attraction (saṃgraha-vastu), the four immeasurables (catur-apramāṇa), and so forth are all categorized as practices for the benefit of others (para-artha). Such diverse practices are boundless (ananta), and all are the superior practices cultivated herein.

title: 成唯識論
text: 論曰：若時菩薩於所緣境，無分別智都無所得，不取種種戲論相故，爾時乃名實住唯識真勝義性，即證真如智與真如平等平等，俱離能取、所取相故，能、所取相，俱是分別，有所得心，戲論現故。
left: The treatise says: When a Bodhisattva (bodhisattva), with regard to an object of cognition (ālambana), possesses non-discriminative wisdom (nirvikalpa-jñāna) and attains absolutely nothing (anupalambha), it is because they do not grasp at the various signs of conceptual proliferation (prapañca). At that time, it is called truly dwelling in the nature of the true ultimate reality (paramārtha) of Consciousness-Only; that is, the wisdom that realizes True Suchness (tathatā) and True Suchness itself are equal and identical, for both are free from the characteristics of the grasper (grāhaka) and the grasped (grāhya). The characteristics of both the grasper and the grasped are conceptual construction (vikalpa), because the mind that attains an object (upalambha) manifests as conceptual proliferation.
right: The treatise says: When a Bodhisattva (bodhisattva), with regard to an object of cognition (ālambana), possesses non-discriminative wisdom (nirvikalpa-jñāna) and attains absolutely nothing, because they do not grasp at the various signs of conceptual proliferation (prapañca), at that time it is called truly dwelling in the nature of the true ultimate reality (paramārtha-svabhāva) of Consciousness-Only (vijñapti-mātra). This is because the wisdom that realizes True Suchness (tathatā) and True Suchness itself are equal and identical, both being free from the characteristics of the grasper (grāhaka) and the grasped (grāhya). The characteristics of the grasper and the grasped are both conceptual constructions (vikalpa), because a mind that attains an object manifests as conceptual proliferation.

title: 成唯識論
text: 如何道諦實能感苦？誰言實感？不爾，如何？無漏定、願，資有漏業，令所得果，相續長時，展轉增勝，假說名感。如是感時，由所知障為緣助力，非獨能感。然所知障，不障解脫，無能發業潤生用故。
left: How does the path-truth (mārgasatya) truly induce suffering? Who says it truly induces it? It is not so. How then? The undefiled meditative absorption (anāsravasamādhi) and aspiration (praṇidhāna) support tainted karma (sāsravakarman), causing the resulting fruit to continue for a long time, extending and increasing in intensity; this is metaphorically called "inducing." When it induces in this way, it is due to the cognitive obstacles (jñeyāvaraṇa) acting as a contributing condition; they cannot induce it alone. However, the cognitive obstacles do not obstruct liberation, because they lack the function of initiating karma or nourishing rebirth.
right: How is it that the truth of the path (mārga-satya) can truly induce suffering? Who says it truly induces it? It is not so. How then? Untainted (anāsrava) meditative concentration and aspiration support tainted (āsrava) action (karma), causing the resulting fruit (phala) to continue (saṃtāna) for a long time (dīrgha-kāla), increasing and flourishing in succession (paramparā); it is metaphorically said to be "inducing." When it induces in this way, it is due to the cognitive obstacles (jñeyāvaraṇa) acting as a contributing condition (pratyaya); they cannot induce it alone. However, the cognitive obstacles do not obstruct liberation (vimokṣa), because they lack the function of initiating action and nourishing rebirth.

title: 阿毘達磨俱舍論
text: 論曰：前已廣說諸煩惱斷，由見諦道及修道故。道唯無漏亦有漏耶？見道應知唯是無漏，修道通二。所以者何？見道速能治三界故。頓斷九品見所斷故，非世間道有此堪能，故見位中道唯無漏。修道有異故通二種，如向所言由見諦故。此所見諦其相云何？頌曰：
left: The treatise says: It has already been extensively explained that the abandonment of all defilements (kleśa) comes about through the path of seeing the truths and the path of cultivation (bhāvanā-mārga). Are these paths only undefiled (anāsrava), or are they also defiled (āsrava)? It should be known that the path of seeing (darśana-mārga) is only undefiled, while the path of cultivation includes both. For what reason? Because the path of seeing is able to swiftly remedy the three realms (traidhātuka). Because it abruptly abandons the nine grades of what is to be abandoned by seeing (darśana-prahā), and the worldly path (laukika-mārga) does not possess this capability, therefore, in the stage of seeing, the path is only undefiled. Because the path of cultivation is different, it includes two kinds (dvividha), as was stated previously regarding the seeing of the truths. What is the nature of these truths that are seen? The verse says:
